answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent deposits its marble into a staking contract—the ledger entry is irrevocably burned. A sybil operator watching that mirror of the chain cannot replay the deposit because the willow-root hash of the spent output is now part of consensus history. One marble, one burn, one trust grant. Split the marble and you split nothing—dust below threshold is rejected. The timestamp is your proof of uniqueness; the burn is your proof of finality.
